answer_control.rule: no control band has dev success - null >= 0.9; fallback: the first control band at the alpha with the largest success - null

patch_plan.arms: exp17_patch: per band, the counterfactual's coordinates copied into the residual at every J++ layer and window position, in the whole residual (full) or the span of 10 vectors: dm_full, dm_jpart, dm_rem, the J++ colour vectors (jpp), a random subspace; on the control band full, jpp, random only
patch_plan.bands: the run's locked dm band, jpp band and in-task control band (read from the locked settings)

windows.start: start colour .. last token (the swap arms' window)
windows.after: the token after the start colour .. last token (primary: the start colour itself, which names s0', is not patched)

patch_plan.items: the test bank's correct h=2 items whose counterfactual (start colour T^-1(s1')) is answered T(s1') clean (arm cf_clean)

tests.P1: patch_jpp - patch_random at the dm band, window after
tests.P2: patch_dm - patch_jpp at the dm band, window after
tests.P3: patch_dm_rem - patch_dm_jpart at the dm band, window after

patch_plan.test_method: paired bootstrap 95% CI (exp15_score.boot_ci), Holm over P1-P3 within run
controls: patch_full at every band and window: the upper bound (window start: the counterfactual itself)
patch_jpp at the control band: the J++ colour span carries the answer late
secondary: every other arm, band and window: CIs only
specificity per arm: per item 1[success] - (1[echo] + 1[start_swap]) / 2, the success rate above that of two other wrong colours (a patch that only scrambles the answer scores ~0)

deviations: Gemma is run with EXP17_LENS=occupied (run key gemma_occupied): every J++ vector and random direction projected onto the subspace holding 99.99% of Gemma's WikiText residual energy and renormalised, because the raw J++ colour vectors keep only 5-20% of their norm there at layers 28-58 (occupied_subspace.json). Qwen's vectors are 99.4-99.7% inside, so the projection would not change Qwen.

Gemma's factual positive control uses the chat template with the instruction 'Complete the sentence with one word. Reply with that word only.' (raw text: 0 of 76 prompts answered); success counts the bare, capitalised or spaced first token.

Stop rule K1 triggers for gemma_occupied (best factual intermediate-swap gain 0.077 < 0.15). With approval, Gemma's swap test is still run on the test bank but is descriptive only: no confirmatory claims from T1-T5 on Gemma.

Gemma's in-task control: no control band reaches success - null >= 0.9 on dev (best 0.565 - 0.087 at b46_58 alpha 8); the recorded fallback (first control band, largest gain) sets both its answer-control arms and its patch control band.

Interchange patching (exp17_patch) added after the main lock and run on dev for both models before this addendum: counterfactual = the same prompt with start colour T^-1(s1'); P1-P3 and the specificity secondary are pre-registered here, before any test-bank patching.
The difference-of-means key directions were fit on dev items, so the dev patching numbers are in-sample for the dm arms; the test-bank patching is out of sample.

exp17_late early (J++ answer swap with nulls at alpha 1-8 in the earlier dev bands) added, dev only. On Qwen it shows J++ colour swaps do not steer this task at layers 24-48 (<= 0.031 vs null <= 0.021), so the J++-band key swap has no in-band positive control; the controlled comparison is at the dm band.
